newsitem.title: UK: EU cuts soft wheat, raises maize import duties.
newsitem.headline: EU cuts soft wheat, raises maize import duties.

text.p: The European Union will on Tuesday cut duties on transatlantic imports of high, medium and low quality soft wheat to 23.68 ecus, 46.46 ecus and 59.31 ecus a tonne respectively, European Commission figures showed.
Duties were previously set at 31.18 ecus, 56.63 ecus and 67.69 ecus a tonne respectively.
The EU will also on Tuesday raise duties on transatlantic imports of maize to 85.92 ecus a tonne, from 81.68 ecus.
Nearby durum wheat import duties will be cut to zero, from 8.87 ecus a tonne. Duties on transatlantic durum wheat imports remain at zero.
The EU will also on Tuesday cut duties on distant imports of barley and rye to 59.65 ecus a tonne, from 67.73 ecus.
But distant sorghum import duties will be raised to 71.59 ecus tonne, from 67.73 ecus.
Sorghum duties, which were previously aligned with those of barley and rye, will be set differently for the next three months.
This is because the sorghum marketing year starts on October 1, instead of July 1 for barley and rye.
